item.title: Pacific Hurricane Polo Is Now a Dangerous Category 5 Off Mexico
item.description: Hurricane Polo has become a dangerous Category 5 storm as it skirts Mexico’s southwest coast, and is expected to bring heavy rain across the region, the US National Hurricane Center said. Polo was about 360 miles (580 kilometers) south-southeast of the port city of Manzanillo, Mexico, with top winds of 160 miles per hour, the hurricane center said in its latest advisory. Polo is forecast to remain just offshore, sparing the country’s coastline another direct strike by a storm at the top of the five-step Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind scale.

item.title: DoorDash to Pay $132 Million in NYC Over Missing Wages
item.description: DoorDash Inc., the leading food-delivery firm in the US, said it agreed to a $131.5 million settlement with New York City to resolve a probe into its compliance with minimum-pay rules for couriers. The settlement, announced Tuesday, includes more than $83 million to resolve a disagreement over how to calculate pay for time that the workers spend online between deliveries, a requirement under the city’s rules. DoorDash is also paying $16.7 million in fines to the city’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, which enforces the pay rule.

item.title: CVC-Backed Home Insurance Firm Bamboo Said to Postpone IPO
item.description: Bamboo Insurance Services Inc., a home insurance firm controlled by private equity firm CVC Capital Partners, has postponed its initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter. Related: Bamboo Insurance Targets $3.24 Billion Valuation in IPO Bamboo was founded in 2018 and valued at $1.75 billion when CVC-advised funds purchased a controlling stake in the firm from White Mountains Insurance Group Ltd. The Midvale, Utah-based company cited market conditions for the move, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public.

Damian dismissed an earlier version of the lawsuit last September.

item.title: Drivers Widely Overestimate Driving Ability Despite Engaging in Risky Habits: Survey

A driving report can help reveal the patterns we may not see in ourselves, giving people a new way to understand how they really drive, not just how they think they drive.” Drivers’ perceptions of risk often differ depending on their own self-reported behavior.

item.title: Electronic Tolling, Better Signage Could Have Prevented Deadly Ohio Toll Plaza Crash
item.description: A deadly crash at a toll plaza on Interstate 80 near Swanton, Ohio, in 2024 could have been avoided if the turnpike used fully electronic tolling and provided clearer information about toll payment options, according to findings by the National Transportation Safety Board. NTSB investigators determined that the toll plaza’s hybrid design, which combines high-speed electronic tolling lanes with separated low-speed manual tolling lanes, increased the risk of a severe crash by creating conditions that encourage last-minute sudden lane changes and large speed differences between vehicles. On August 15, 2024, a crash occured the Swanton Township Toll Plaza on the Ohio Turnpike.

item.title: US property claims severity and costs rising, even with stable designated cat events: Verisk
item.description: Property insurance claims severity and costs are rising in the United States, even during periods where the number of catastrophe events designated were stable. CAT claims now account for 43% of Q2 volume, up from 34% five years ago, even though the number of PCS® designated events has held steady.” At the same time, claim severity in US property insurance is following a typical maturity trend, which suggests the average claim cost for Q2 2026 may be one of the highest seen, despite the perceived reduction in cat losses that are much discussed across insurance, reinsurance and ILS markets. In its latest quarterly property report, Verisk explains that, “Property and reconstruction spend is consolidating into fewer, higher cost claims.” While claim assignment volumes fell in the second-quarter, a period that typically sees meaningful severe weather activity across the United States, Verisk notes that “average severity is tracking toward the highest quarterly level in recent years.” This means fewer claims to manage, but higher costs associated with each one, on average.

item.title: Strengthening Hurricane Polo brings Mexico catastrophe bond into focus
item.description: Hurricane Polo is rapidly intensifying off the southwestern coast of Mexico and the strengthening trend is expected to continue, while the track remains uncertain at this time, which has brought the $175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric catastrophe bond into focus this week. Any deviation closer to the coastline of Mexico could take hurricane Polo very near to the IBRD Mexico 2024 catastrophe bond’s parametric trigger box arrangement, which runs up the coastline. However, the current location of hurricane Polo is close to the Mexican coastline and any wobble in the path as the storm moves forwards could bring it much closer to the coastline and the parametric box of the catastrophe bond, which runs just off the shore.

item.title: Polo Strengthens Into Hurricane, Threatening Mexico’s Pacific Resort Towns
item.description: Polo strengthened off Mexico’s Pacific coast into a hurricane on Monday and is forecast to rapidly intensify into a major storm, threatening floods, dangerous surf and strong wind gusts in coastal states and near major beach resorts. Around mid-day locally (1800 GMT), Polo was located some 270 miles (435 km) south-southeast of port city Manzanillo and 190 miles (305 km) south-southwest of tourist town Zihuatanejo, packing maximum sustained winds of 80 mph (130 km/h), the US National Hurricane Center said. Accuweather also warned that tropical moisture from Mexico is expected to push north through the rest of the week, threatening flash floods in the US Southwest.

item.title: Australian State Bans Data Centers From Residential Areas
item.description: One of Australia’s largest states has banned the construction of data centers in residential areas and mandated that they must “bring their own renewable energy supply,” part of a slew of rules designed to tackle growing community pushback. In addition, data centers will not be allowed in residential areas, with a mandatory buffer zone of 150 meters (164 yards) from any houses. The state of Victoria, home to Melbourne, announced on Tuesday that while data centers were vital to the economy, they would need to take steps to ensure local water and electricity resources were not significantly impacted.

item.title: FAA Resolves Air Traffic Outage That Snarled Northeast Travel
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration said it’s resolved the equipment outage at an air traffic facility in Philadelphia that severely disrupted air travel in the Northeast, leading to hundreds of flights being canceled. The travel chaos overshadowed the rollout of the FAA’s new AI air traffic tool, known as SMART, which is designed to identify areas where congestion or weather could disrupt travel and recommend changes to reduce delays and cancellations. The outage occurred after the failure of the primary circuit at a Philadelphia facility that guides flights into and out of major hubs, including Newark Liberty International Airport and Philadelphia International Airport.

item.title: Tesla Faces Major Trial for Alleged Bias Against Black Workers, After Years of Lawsuits
item.description: Tesla’s high profile and the thousands of workers involved in the case make it among the most significant involving employment discrimination claims against a major US company to go to trial in recent years. A California agency’s lawsuit accusing Tesla of allowing rampant race discrimination at its flagship assembly plant is set to go to trial on Monday, one of a series of similar lawsuits being faced by the electric vehicle maker. In the lawsuit filed in 2022, the California Civil Rights Department claims Black workers at Tesla’s Fremont, California plant were subjected to pervasive harassment by other employees, including racial slurs and graffiti, and Tesla failed to prevent or stop it.
